title: Impressionism
examples: What was the main difference between Impressionist and earlier art?
Can you show me an example of Monet's work?

explain.say: Today we will learn about Impressionism in art.

items: Focus on light and everyday life

explain.say: Claude Monet was a very famous Impressionist painter.
Impressionists focused on capturing the effect of light.
They used quick, visible brushstrokes to show movement.

items: Step 2: Use quick dabs of paint

explain.say: Painting outdoors, or plein air, was a big change.
In real life, think about photographing a sunset.

faq.q: What was the Impressionist movement really about?
faq.a: It was about capturing the fleeting moment and the changing effects of light. It moved away from historical or mythological subjects.
asks: What did they want to paint?
Were they painting feelings or things?

faq.q: Why did they use visible brushstrokes?
faq.a: The quick strokes helped show the vibration and movement of light in the air. It made the painting feel immediate and alive.
While painting outdoors, or plein air, was key, they could also study light effects in studios. But the outdoor experience was central.
asks: Where did they paint their best work?

faq.q: Is Monet the only Impressionist painter?
faq.a: No, many artists were part of the movement, like Renoir and Degas. They all shared an interest in modern life and light.

faq.q: What is the difference between Impressionism and Realism?
faq.a: Realism focused on depicting everyday life exactly as it was seen, while Impressionism focused on the effect of light on that scene.
asks: Is it the same as painting what you see?
How is it different from photography?

facts: Impressionism focused on modern life and everyday scenes.
Artists often painted the same subject at different times to show light changes.
Plein air means painting outdoors, which was a new practice.
The visible brushstrokes are a key characteristic of the style.

quiz.say: Which element did Impressionists try to capture most?
quiz.why: The entire movement was built around observing how light altered colors in nature.

wrong.0: This was the focus of older, more formal art styles.
wrong.1: The visible brushstrokes were a deliberate part of their technique.
wrong.2: They preferred painting ordinary people and landscapes.

quiz.say: If an artist paints a haystack at sunrise and then again at noon, what are they showing?
quiz.why: This shows their interest in capturing the specific quality of light at different times.

wrong.0: While mood matters, the subject was the physical light itself.
wrong.2: The size remained the same, but the light changed everything.
wrong.3: The focus was on the structure illuminated by the sun.

quiz.say: When painting outdoors, what did the Impressionists need to pay attention to?
quiz.why: They were capturing the feeling of being there at that exact moment.

wrong.0: They noticed the reflections and the surrounding air too.
wrong.1: The light often blurred the edges, which they captured.
wrong.2: Their focus was more on objective visual reality than deep personal emotion.
